title: Kevin Feige pushes back on Connor Storrie Ghost Rider rumor
body_md:
Marvel Studios executive Kevin Feige has responded to a report linking Connor Storrie with a potential Ghost Rider project. According to coverage published on November 26, 2026, Feige addressed the subject while speaking with Entertainment Weekly during promotion for Avengers: Doomsday. He characterized the casting rumor as lacking creativity, casting doubt on the report without announcing an alternative lineup.

The original report described Storrie as being considered for a project associated with Shawn Levy and Ryan Gosling. However, the available information does not establish that Storrie has signed a contract or that the proposed creative team has been officially confirmed. Feige's response should therefore not be treated as a comprehensive production announcement or definitive evidence of another actor's involvement.

The comments are noteworthy because Marvel executives do not routinely respond publicly to every casting rumor. Even a brief reaction can generate substantial discussion among fans. Nevertheless, an ambiguous response from a studio executive cannot independently establish the status of negotiations or reveal details that have not been publicly disclosed.

Ghost Rider occupies a distinctive place in Marvel's comic book universe. Stories involving the character frequently combine supernatural mythology with questions of responsibility, punishment and the consequences of extraordinary powers. Multiple characters have carried the identity, including Johnny Blaze and Robbie Reyes. Until the intended version is identified, speculation about a particular actor remains incomplete.

Nicolas Cage previously portrayed Johnny Blaze in two theatrical Ghost Rider movies. Gabriel Luna subsequently played Robbie Reyes in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. Those adaptations demonstrate that the identity can support different protagonists, settings and storytelling approaches. A new interpretation would not necessarily reproduce the same narrative or casting choices.

From a creative perspective, another Ghost Rider adaptation could provide an opportunity to explore Marvel's supernatural mythology in greater depth. That possibility is an observation about the character's storytelling potential, not confirmation that the proposed project will connect with any particular film or television series.

The historical feed contains only a summary of the interview coverage rather than the complete conversation. Consequently, it would be inappropriate to attribute additional explanations or specific production details to Feige beyond those supplied in the report. The clearest established development is his skeptical reaction to the rumor involving Storrie.

For audiences following Marvel's future slate, the distinction between an intriguing casting report and an official announcement remains essential. The project's eventual cast, production schedule and release plans will require further confirmation from the studio. Until then, the possibility of a new Ghost Rider interpretation remains a subject of discussion rather than a settled casting outcome.
excerpt: Marvel’s Kevin Feige questions a casting rumor without confirming the film’s lineup.
